payload.action: use removesuffix for suffixes; rstrip only for character classes
payload.claim: str.rstrip(suffix) strips a character SET, not a suffix: 'mypy'.rstrip('.py') is 'm'

payload.action: lint the whole repo with an explicit --config ruff.toml
payload.claim: enforce/pyproject.toml makes ruff treat enforce/ as its own project, so a repo-root lint silently uses two configs

payload.action: cache an expensive constructor with lru_cache when it is called per item
payload.claim: count_tokens rebuilt the tiktoken encoding per call, which took validation from under a second to 66

payload.action: normalize date objects to isoformat after yaml.safe_load, rather than demanding quotes
payload.claim: YAML parses an unquoted ISO date into a date object, so a string-typed schema field rejects it

payload.action: make every correction in discipline/, never in sources/
payload.claim: sources/ holds the superseded originals; they contain ~35 known contradictions

payload.action: run build_index.py before build_graph.py
payload.claim: build_index refreshes token counts that build_graph then reads, so building the graph first leaves it stale

payload.action: keep GENERATE_HTML = YES in any Doxyfile used only for checking
payload.claim: Doxygen reports fully documented functions as undocumented when no HTML output is generated; XML alone is not enough

payload.action: use ## for module constants and class attributes, never #:
payload.claim: Doxygen ignores Sphinx's #: attribute comments entirely; only ## opens a documentation block

payload.action: escape it as \@ or wrap the name in backticks when naming a decorator in prose
payload.claim: a bare @ in docstring prose is parsed as a Doxygen command, so '@overload' produced 'documented symbol decorator was not declared'

payload.action: leave EXTRACT_ALL = NO in any Doxyfile used as a gate
payload.claim: EXTRACT_ALL = YES silently disables WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED, switching off the check it looks like it strengthens

payload.task: vendoring integration into top-level agent configuration

payload.action: run integrate.py after vendoring; copying is not announcing
payload.claim: vendor.py install copies the discipline but nothing under .agent/ is loaded by an agent session on its own

payload.action: re-run vendor.py install after any upstream tool change, before testing the target
payload.claim: a vendored tool is a snapshot: fixing tools/integrate.py upstream does not fix the copy already installed in a target repo

payload.action: compare parsed objects, not file text, when checking that settings were preserved
payload.claim: round-tripping .claude/settings.json through json.dumps re-indents it, producing a diff with no content change

payload.action: delete the docstring node instead, and only append Pass if the body would be empty
payload.claim: replacing a docstring with ast.Pass when fingerprinting makes ADDING a docstring change the body length, so every documented function falsely reads as a code change

triggers.pattern: the code changed, not just its documentation

payload.action: rebuild the baseline from the pre-migration commit with git archive, not from the working tree
payload.claim: correcting a fingerprinting bug mid-migration invalidates the baseline, and re-recording from the working tree would bake in whatever agents already changed

payload.action: strip \x1b[...m before matching, rather than trying to disable colour
payload.claim: ruff emits ANSI colour to a pipe and ignores NO_COLOR, so any tool parsing its output must strip escape codes

payload.action: before dispatching, extract the deterministic substitutions into a script and give agents only the part that needs judgment
payload.claim: splitting a migration into a scripted mechanical half and an agent-authored judgment half kept every agent at a low allocation tier

payload.action: build the verifier before the fan-out, so each agent's contract is one command rather than a judgment
payload.claim: a single deterministic stop condition lowered the tier of 13 parallel agents more than any prompt wording did

payload.task: Document every element in tools/ and enforce/checks/ to Doxygen form, then close the gate

payload.action: Leave WARN_NO_PARAMDOC off and let enforce/checks/doc_coverage.py decide DOC-007 completeness by reading the return annotation.
payload.claim: Doxygen's WARN_NO_PARAMDOC does not treat a Python '-> None' annotation as void, so it demands an @return from every procedure.

triggers.pattern: return type of member .* is not documented

payload.action: Leave WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED off; doc_coverage decides DOC-001/DOC-002 presence at the declaration site.
payload.claim: Doxygen re-reports an already-documented dataclass field as undocumented when a method reads it bare as self.field, pointing at the use rather than the declaration.

triggers.pattern: Member .* \(variable\) of class .* is not documented

payload.action: Write the period outside the span. doc_style reports it under DOC-010 with the span named.
payload.claim: A Doxygen code span ending in a single period, as `foo.`, aborts the comment block and is reported only as an unclosed </tt>, naming neither file location nor cause.

triggers.pattern: end of comment block while expecting command </tt>

payload.action: Ignore multiple-leading-hashes-for-block-comment in the canonical enforce/pyproject.toml, not just locally: every adopting project hits this on its first documented constant.
payload.claim: ruff's E266 forbids the ## block form that DOC-002 requires for elements Python gives no docstring slot; the two rules cannot both be obeyed.

payload.action: Keep an enforce/ruff.toml that extends ../ruff.toml, so a vendored template never doubles as live configuration.
payload.claim: ruff configures each file from its nearest ancestor config, so enforce/pyproject.toml -- which is the template consumers copy -- was silently linting everything under enforce/ instead of the root ruff.toml.

payload.action: Pair every documentation-writing agent with a reviewer that verifies each claim against the code it describes; presence and truth are separate properties needing separate mechanisms.
payload.claim: A presence-only documentation gate passes happily on documentation that is confidently false: a review stage over the same 13 batches found 90 wrong claims and 59 filler docstrings that the gate had already accepted.

payload.action: In docgate.strip_documentation, delete the docstring node and pad an emptied body with Pass; never substitute in place.
payload.claim: A behaviour oracle that substitutes a placeholder for a removed docstring changes the body length, so adding a docstring registers as a behaviour change; deleting the node instead is what makes the AST comparison sound.

triggers.pattern: the code changed, not just its documentation

payload.action: Generate Python source with the Edit/Write tools rather than a heredoc. enforce/fitness/test_meta.py now fails on any control character in source.
payload.claim: A Bash heredoc on this machine collapses a doubled backslash, so Python source generated that way turned a regex \b into a literal backspace; the check kept passing its own tests and silently over-reported 400 findings.

payload.action: Query learn.py retrieve --file/--error at the START of a gate run and on the first failing diagnostic, not at the end of the session when learnings are written. An un-queried database is indistinguishable from an empty one.
payload.claim: The learning database already held the ruff config-shadowing defect (L-0002) before this session rediscovered it independently; retrieval was sound, but nothing prompted a query before the gate was run.

payload.action: Treat the Doxygen run as the mechanism covering ## block form, and do not assume an AST check that walks docstrings has seen the ## comments beside them.
payload.claim: doc_style reads docstrings only, so it cannot police the form of a ## block; the comment documenting the trailing-period trap was itself written with the trap in it and only the Doxygen gate caught it.

payload.task: Implement converged items 3-10: enforcement status, V080 ratchet, learn verify, write-verify doctrine, cross-platform CI, doxygen version pin, hash-block content rules, baseline provenance, ruff sweep

payload.action: Derive the ceiling from the recorded evidence set, or validate the two against each other on load. A baseline that is trusted rather than checked is not a ratchet.
payload.claim: A ratchet whose ceiling is a hand-editable integer, not cross-checked against the evidence list beside it, is disabled by a one-character edit: setting the count to 500 against 106 real pairs made validate.py exit 0.

payload.action: Stamp a working-tree sentinel when the file differs from the ref, and pin it with a test that replays every entry against the ref it names.
payload.claim: A provenance field that records the checked-out commit unconditionally is false for every file fingerprinted from a dirty tree, and it defeats the audit it exists to enable: 15 entries claimed a commit at which their fingerprints did not exist.

payload.action: Split on underscores before splitting on case, and prove the rule fires on a constant, not only on a lowercase field. This silenced DOC-009 on exactly the elements ## blocks document.
payload.claim: A restates-the-name check that splits an identifier before each capital is inert on ALL-CAPS names: MAX_RETRIES becomes eleven single letters, so no summary can ever be a subset of it.

payload.action: Read a green test suite as evidence that the tests pass, never that the gate passes. Either assert success per gate entry or publish the per-entry status; a gate nobody fails is a gate nobody runs.
payload.claim: This repository's own gate does not pass and never has: ruff check exits 1 with 269 findings, while the fitness test that covers the gate asserts only returncode in (0,1) -- that each command starts, not that it succeeds -- so pytest stays green over a failing gate entry.

payload.action: Never let the agent that built a mechanism be the one that certifies it. Budget an independent verifier per batch and give it named failure modes to hunt rather than asking it to review.
payload.claim: Nine parallel agents each claimed complete=true and passed their own acceptance commands; an independent adversarial verifier then found three real defects, one of which was a systematically false audit field in the very artefact built to prevent laundering.

payload.action: Keep every copy-me configuration under enforce/templates/, a directory holding no Python, so it is an ancestor of nothing either tool processes; never shadow a template with a second live config.
payload.claim: A ruff/pytest config file inside a vendored directory is discovered from the nearest ancestor, so a template carrying [tool.ruff] or [tool.pytest.ini_options] governs the host repository's files; a shim extending a relative parent path fixes it upstream and breaks ruff outright once vendored, because the parent it names does not exist under .agent/.

payload.action: Exclude every tool cache directory from the vendored set, and gitignore .ruff_cache/ and .mypy_cache/ as .pytest_cache/ already was.
payload.claim: vendor.py's SKIP_DIRS excluded __pycache__ and .pytest_cache but not .ruff_cache, so 18 cache files written beside the template configuration were copied into .agent/ and hashed into MANIFEST.json, making the version stamp depend on what had been run in the checkout.

payload.action: When packaging a vendored tree, write an explicit zip directory entry for every directory that holds no file at any depth.
payload.claim: vendor.py creates .agent/overrides/ empty, and a zip built only from file members silently drops it, so unzipping a release yields an install that vendor.py check itself calls broken.

payload.action: Assert the baseline's key set equals the covered Python files rather than asserting a count, so a covered file that is never baselined fails instead of passing.
payload.claim: Two of the 31 files the documentation gate covers (tools/test_docgate.py, tools/test_mechanism_checks.py) had no baseline entry at all, so the behaviour oracle silently verified nothing for them; a hard-coded entry count in test_docgate.py hid it.

payload.action: Excuse those files per pattern name with a written reason in release.py ALLOWED, never by exempting test files wholesale.
payload.claim: A leak scan over the shipped tree fires on proof-of-failure fixtures for learn.py's own credential guard and on the AST fingerprints of those fixtures in tools/doc_baseline.json, which are synthetic by construction.

payload.action: Limit a validator's resolution roots to what the release actually ships, and prove the exclusion with a proof-of-failure test
payload.claim: A self-check that resolves references through a tree the release does not ship is green in the development repository and red in every vendored install
payload.verification: python tools/vendor.py install TMP && python TMP/.agent/tools/validate.py

payload.action: Pass newline= explicitly on both read_text and write_text whenever a file's existing bytes are part of the contract
payload.claim: Path.write_text without newline= rewrites every LF to CRLF on Windows, so integrate.py cannot honour its documented byte-preservation contract there

payload.action: Compare bytes, not decoded text, in any test whose oracle is byte preservation
payload.claim: A test that round-trips through read_text and write_text normalises line endings on both sides, so it cannot detect the newline corruption its name claims to prove absent

payload.action: Record what was added at apply time, or leave shared-valued entries in place on removal
payload.claim: Removing configuration entries by value cannot distinguish an entry the integrator added from an identical one the host already had, so uninstall destroys host configuration

payload.action: Regenerate the mirror with tools/build_skill_mirror.py --check before trusting anything under references/, and add its --check to enforce/fitness/test_meta.py::GATE (and .github/workflows/gate.yml, kept in sync by hand).
payload.claim: The .claude/skills/python-discipline/references/ mirror can be generated verbatim (whole-tree file copy) from discipline/, mirroring build_index.py's Artifact/--check pattern; SKILL.md is hand-authored and adapted, never part of the copy.

payload.action: Read and write host-owned files with newline='' on both sides, and assert preservation on read_bytes against the original bytes, driven from a pure-LF fixture as well as a pure-CRLF one -- on Windows the CRLF case passes by accident.
payload.claim: On Windows, reading a file with Path.read_text and writing it back with Path.write_text rewrites every line ending in it: read_text folds CRLF to LF and write_text expands LF to os.linesep, so a pure-LF host file comes back with a CR on every line while every assertion made on decoded text still passes.

payload.action: Record at apply time which entries were genuinely absent beforehand, in a file outside the directories vendor.py replaces wholesale, and remove only those; with no record, remove nothing and print which entries were left and why.
payload.claim: An uninstall that identifies its own contributions by value cannot distinguish an entry it added from an identical one the host already had, so it silently deletes host configuration; integrate.py --remove destroyed a pre-existing Bash(pytest:*) permission this way.

payload.action: When a test names a byte-level or encoding-level property, drive it from bytes and assert on bytes; before citing a test as evidence in a document, run it against the unfixed code and confirm it fails.
payload.claim: A test named for a property can fail to check it: test_an_existing_file_keeps_every_byte_it_had wrote its fixture with write_text and read it back with read_text, normalising both sides, and was cited in shipped documentation as evidence for byte preservation.

payload.action: Write the qualified name as prose (the Artifact shape in tools/build_index.py) instead of path::Name, and run a real doxygen build over tools/ before declaring the documentation gate green
payload.claim: A code span of the form path::Name in a docstring makes Doxygen 1.10.0 emit an unresolvable explicit-link error, which docgate does not catch because it runs no Doxygen stage

payload.action: Split the two names across separate spans: write the Name in one span and the module path in another, never joined by a double colon inside a single span.
payload.claim: Doxygen 1.10.0 reads a code span of the form path::Name as an explicit link request and fails the build when it cannot resolve it, so a docstring citing another module's class inside one span breaks the documentation gate.

payload.action: Pin tiktoken in the environment and rebuild the corpus as one change, or correct meta/SCHEMA.md, KERNEL.md and README.md which all claim the field is tiktoken-measured
payload.claim: Committed tokens: values across the corpus are the len(text)/3.7 fallback estimate, not tiktoken measurements, because tiktoken is absent from the claude env; installing it would rewrite every module and cascade into graph.json

payload.action: Require a word boundary and a common-identifier stop-list in environment_literals, with a proof-of-failure test that a host named main still builds
payload.claim: tools/release.py derives blocking leak patterns from platform.node(), so a machine whose hostname is a common word (this one is MAIN) matches def main/__main__ everywhere and the release build aborts

payload.action: Invoke the claude conda env interpreter explicitly for every gate command; verify the interpreter before trusting a green run
payload.claim: A bare python on this machine resolves to the miniforge base env, which has no pytest, jsonschema or ruff plugins, so a gate run against it decides nothing and looks like it passed

payload.action: Run the GATE tuple before staging and refuse on any non-zero step; keep the tuple in one importable module so the release and the fitness test cannot disagree
payload.claim: release.py had three gates that all ask whether the archive is well formed and none that asks whether the corpus it was cut from passes its own gate, so an archive was buildable from a tree with stale artifacts and failing tests

payload.action: Keep a PROTECTED set checked before the baseline is consulted, and a test asserting every protected code is tied to a rule by a mechanism tag, the template or ENFORCEMENT.md
payload.claim: A lint ratchet must refuse any ruff code that decides a binding rule even when that code is already in the baseline, or a future baseline move silently switches a rule's mechanism off

payload.action: Ignore non-imperative-mood in the template with the conflict written down, keeping the summary-line rules on; do not reword accessor docstrings to satisfy it
payload.claim: ruff D401 and DOC-009 cannot both be obeyed on an accessor: D401 demands an imperative where DOC-009 asks for the noun phrase that states what the value IS, and the imperative narrates the mechanism DOC-009 rejects

payload.action: Keep the code and the rule id on separate lines when a template comment describes a conflict rather than an enforcement
payload.claim: build_graph derives triggered_by edges from a ruff code and a rule id appearing on the SAME comment line in the enforcement template, so a comment explaining that a code CONFLICTS with a rule mints a false enforcement edge

payload.action: Read a layer alias map from [tool.agent-discipline]; a project renames its layers, and a run under a narrowed declaration announces what it left inactive
payload.claim: layer_of matched four literal segment names, so a project laying out cli/composition/services had those files resolve to no layer and every layer-scoped check skipped them WHILE REPORTING CLEAN -- a silence indistinguishable from conformance

payload.action: Split presence from form -- DOC-001/003 universal, DOC-002/007 conditional on a declared doc_engine, and DOC-014 makes the declaration itself binding so an undeclared project is never mistaken for a conformant one
payload.claim: DOC-002 and DOC-007 mandated one engine's punctuation for every adopter: on 6,700 lines documented in Sphinx style they produced 1,064 findings of form against 18 of substance, burying the real ones

payload.action: Decide check membership by what a module defines -- a class deriving from Check -- read from the AST, never by directory position
payload.claim: Adding a non-check module to enforce/checks/ minted a phantom check:project mechanism node, because build_graph and test_meta both assumed every module there was a mechanism

payload.action: Use [tool.importlinter] in a standalone toml, and run every named mechanism at least once against real code before recording it as external
payload.claim: enforce/importlinter.toml used a [importlinter] section where import-linter requires [tool.importlinter], so it parsed as nothing and reported 'Could not read any configuration' -- the eight ARCH/DEP/EFCT/API rules it decides were marked external while the tool never loaded

payload.action: Declare each port's failure modes beside its Protocol, as ARCH-007 already requires the contract to state error modes; adapters raise them and the core catches them without knowing adapters exist
payload.claim: A port's error type belongs to the port, not to adapters: filing it under adapters/ forced the app layer to import adapters to catch a failure, which ARCH-001 flagged as an outward import

payload.action: Exempt the composition root from transitive-reach contracts and say why in the contract file
payload.claim: An ARCH-004 contract forbidding a layer transitive reach to a foreign dependency cannot bind the composition root, which necessarily reaches whatever the adapters it wires import -- ARCH-004 and ARCH-011 would be jointly unsatisfiable

payload.action: Partition positionally rather than by value membership, and compare partitions as multisets in the property
payload.claim: A property suite found a partition defect no hand-written example could reach: plan_prune used value membership to compute the complement, which collapses two equal entries; the store cannot hold one path twice so nobody would have written that case

payload.action: Scope the plan/apply obligation to the deciding layers (app, shell) and exclude adapters, the same shape as ARCH-004 having to exempt the composition root
payload.claim: EFCT-005 mechanized over the adapter layer reports every port delete primitive as ungated destruction -- six correct functions across three real packages plus the reference's own LocalFileStore.delete; an adapter IS the apply half of plan/apply

triggers.pattern: with no plan and no opt-in

payload.action: Calibrate every new check against a conformant tree and an unrelated real tree before recording its baseline, and require both a must-fire and a must-not-fire case
payload.claim: A check that finds nothing across 6,700 lines of independently written code is a suspect, not a success: three of eight new checks reported zero and only the must-fire companions distinguished a working check from a dead one

payload.action: Open every test module with Oracle: <contract|property|differential|golden|example>; the closed list is what makes 'oracle: the tests pass' unwritable
payload.claim: 28 of 29 test files in a real hexagonal project declare no oracle, so their assertions rest on whatever the implementation produced when they were written

payload.action: Split the Check base into ModuleCheck and TextCheck so a rule whose subject is markdown, JSONL or any generated file can have a mechanism at all
payload.claim: Ten binding rules (ALLOC-002..009, TEAMS-001/002) were unmechanizable only because the check framework could parse nothing but Python, and a dispatch record is markdown -- the rules are not about source

payload.action: Read the tier and the effort separately, each at its maximum over the whole record; the word boundary keeps a signal score like E=2 from being read as an effort tier
payload.claim: A dispatch record states the mechanical allocation and then the escalation that overrides it, so reading only the first T/E pair reported three correct records as under-allocated -- and the escalation is often written as a bare E2, not in T/E form

payload.action: Try the operation and handle its failure; reserve the probe for acting on absence, which does not race
payload.claim: Eight look-before-you-leap races in real code, every one the shape if p.exists(): p.unlink() -- the file can vanish between the question and the answer, and the handler needed anyway is the one that would have worked

payload.action: Write the must-not-fire case for the most common correct idiom the check could mistake, not just any conformant sample
payload.claim: A check's accepting case is what keeps it usable: acting on absence and a literal getattr are both common and correct, and a check reporting either would be switched off within a day

payload.action: Narrow a text pattern to the thing that actually breaks the property -- a clock reading or an explicit generation stamp, not any date -- and pin each calibration case as a must-not-fire test so the narrowing cannot be re-derived away
payload.claim: Two checks reported correct files on their first run because the pattern was too literal: a bare date in generated output is data rather than a generation stamp, and a rule module about generation matched its own router keyword 'generated file'

payload.action: Author any file containing quotes or backslashes with the Write or Edit tool, never a shell heredoc -- the same remedy L-0026 recorded for a different symptom of the same cause
payload.claim: A bash heredoc failed twice this session on content containing triple quotes and backslash escapes, once mangling regex escapes into a SyntaxWarning and once aborting the whole command; neither corrupted a file but both wasted a step

triggers.pattern: unexpected EOF while looking for matching

payload.action: After widening docgate.COVERED, run pytest tools/test_docgate.py rather than trusting a green 'docgate --all'; a covered-but-unbaselined file is invisible to the gate itself.
payload.claim: docgate --all passes on a newly covered file that has no baseline entry at all, because there is no prior fingerprint to compare against; only the roster test in tools/test_docgate.py notices the gap.

payload.action: Write or edit any file containing quotes or backslash escapes with the Write/Edit tools; never through a heredoc.
payload.claim: Authoring Python that contains backslash escapes through a bash heredoc mangled '\n' into real newlines and produced a file with 262 syntax errors -- the third recurrence of L-0026 this session.

payload.action: Suppress a ruff finding with '# ruff: ignore[rule-name] - reason' using the long rule name, never '# noqa'.
payload.claim: Ruff in this environment treats '# noqa: CODE' as a defect and expects '# ruff: ignore[rule-name]'; converting the repository's suppressions to noqa introduced 6 new findings and suppressed nothing.

payload.action: When a new directory holds mechanisms, add it to docgate.COVERED in the same change that creates it, and baseline every file in it.
payload.claim: docgate.COVERED named enforce/checks but not enforce/fitness, so 13 fitness suites -- mechanisms in exactly the same sense -- were written entirely outside the gate that keeps their documentation true; widening it immediately found three undocumented module constants.

payload.action: Never wire import-linter into a gate as 'python -m importlinter.cli'. Call the API: configure(), read_user_options(), _register_contract_types(), create_report() -- and assert the contract count, because a config that resolves nothing reports '0 broken'.
payload.claim: python -m importlinter.cli exits 0 having checked nothing: the module has no __main__ guard, so it imports and returns success. Only the console script works, and it is not reachable from sys.executable.

payload.action: Evict the root packages from sys.modules before building an import graph over a specific tree, and restore them after. A green contract run over a tree you did not analyse is a false pass.
payload.claim: import-linter resolves its root packages by import, and sys.modules is consulted before sys.path -- so with the package already imported by another test, contracts run against the tree imported FIRST and a deliberately broken copy came back '7 kept'.

payload.action: Do not pin or gate on mutmut in a Windows-hosted repository. TEST-013 stays external and undecided; record that rather than implying a tool runs.
payload.claim: mutmut 3.3.1 cannot run on Windows at all: mutmut/__main__.py does an unconditional module-scope 'import resource', which is Unix-only, so it raises ModuleNotFoundError before parsing an argument.

payload.action: Run both checkers, not one. OPEN-005's reasoning is empirical, not stylistic -- the second checker paid for itself on first contact with the reference.
payload.claim: pyright strict found two defects in the reference package that mypy --strict reported clean: a frozenset whose element type was Unknown, and a redundant isinstance concealing an exhaustiveness guard that decided nothing.

payload.action: Any vendored tool with a default target must detect a vendored install and refuse the default rather than checking the shipped fixture. A false pass is worse than no check because it is reported as evidence.
payload.claim: vendor.py ships all of tools/ and all of enforce/, so an adopter receives import_gate.py and type_gate.py alongside the reference package they default to -- running them in an adopter repo would have reported green about a package the adopter did not write.

payload.action: Resolve the final path component by stem as well as by name, and keep CANONICAL_LAYERS complete. A layer-scoped check that finds nothing reads exactly like a check that finds nothing wrong.
payload.claim: layer_of matched directory segments only, so a shell written as cli.py and composition.py at the package root resolved to 'unknown' and every layer-scoped check skipped 8 files silently. Separately, 'ports' was absent from CANONICAL_LAYERS, so every ports/ file also answered 'unknown'.

payload.action: When a rule forbids a foreign type, check inheritance as well as annotation -- inheriting is how a domain actually acquires a framework, and is strictly worse than annotating.
payload.claim: ARCH-013 listed BaseModel in FOREIGN_TYPES but examined only function signatures, so four domains modelled entirely in pydantic.BaseModel produced zero findings. import-linter's ARCH-004 contract caught the same coupling from the graph side, which is the only reason it was noticed.

payload.action: Exempt names that provably cannot perform the forbidden act, and pair every exemption with a must-still-fire companion. Telling a careful author to stop using the tool built for their situation is how a check loses its reader.
payload.claim: A rule mechanized on the module name over-reports on code that uses only a module's pure members: ARCH-002 fired on PurePosixPath, which cannot touch a disk by construction, and on datetime.date imported as a type.

payload.action: Require a condition to read an environment, argv or a switch-named variable before a literal inside it counts as test detection.
payload.claim: ARCH-012 flagged 'zone == "test"' in a domain that classifies source files into zones. A string literal is not a test signal; a test signal is something the environment tells the program.

payload.action: Give any module documented as runnable an entry point, and test that the runner can fail. This is the same defect the file's own comments describe in lint-imports and mypy, in the one place that exists to prevent it.
payload.claim: tools/gate.py was documented as the way to run the gate and did nothing: the module held the GATE tuple and no __main__ block, so 'python tools/gate.py' imported, printed nothing and exited 0 -- indistinguishable from nine passing steps.

payload.action: Locate a native tool beside the interpreter -- Library/bin on Windows, bin on POSIX -- before falling back to PATH. Same lesson as the ruff finding that let 766 lint findings hide behind a green run.
payload.claim: A conda-installed native binary is on PATH only while the environment is ACTIVATED; every gate step here invokes sys.executable directly, so doxygen was installed correctly and test_doxygen_version_matches_recorded still skipped, verifying nothing.

payload.action: Run the commands a document states, not just read them. Every numeric claim in README was also stale by a full phase -- rules, mechanisms, lint count, covered files, learnings.
payload.claim: CLAUDE.md's post-edit rebuild sequence omitted build_skill_mirror.py, so a maintainer following it exactly would pass all four documented commands and then fail the gate's fifth step on a stale mirror.

payload.action: When a lock format gains a new kind of entry, make the unrecognised case an ERROR rather than a no-match. check_env now reports any conda pin it has no verifier for.
payload.claim: A conda pin written with a single '=' matched neither check_env's pip pattern nor its loose-range pattern, so adding one would have declared a dependency the lock silently did not cover.

payload.action: Index the error vocabulary an agent actually sees, not only the vocabulary this repository's own gate emits. The Prime Directive says 'from the program's own output'; a traceback IS the program's own output.
payload.claim: The graph indexes 17 error triggers, all of them ruff codes and import-linter contract names. It indexes no mypy error code, no Python exception type and no pytest failure shape -- so nav.py context returns a completely empty plan for a traceback, which is the output an agent most often meets.

payload.action: Measure the artefact the corpus controls -- the reading plan -- rather than simulating an agent. It is repeatable, free, and it is the thing a change to the corpus actually moves.
payload.claim: Recovery cost can be measured deterministically without an agent in the loop: nav.py --json reports tokens_planned and per-seed hops, so the reading plan itself is the measurable quantity and it is identical on every run.

payload.action: When something has failed, run diagnose, not context. Reserve context for before you write, when nothing has failed and the question really is what to read.
payload.claim: A reading plan and a diagnosis are different questions with a 88x cost difference: nav.py context returns ~4,994 tokens of modules to read, nav.py diagnose returns the governing rules' own words for a median of 57.

payload.action: Derive a register rather than asking for one, and fail closed when the tree imports something the register does not name. A check with nothing to say is indistinguishable from a check that found nothing wrong.
payload.claim: enforce/importlinter.toml shipped ARCH-004 with an empty forbidden_modules list, which forbids nothing and passes on every tree forever -- and carried a comment saying an empty list merely meant nothing was registered yet, which made the vacuity read as deliberate.

payload.action: Match a keyword by half its topic-bearing stems rather than verbatim, and hold the looseness with reject cases: a router answering 'renaming a variable' with five law modules is as useless as one answering nothing.
payload.claim: The router matched multi-word load_when keywords VERBATIM, so 'adding a new dependency' reached nothing where 'add a dependency' was the trigger. Eight of fifteen realistic task queries routed to an empty answer, which sends the agent to read speculatively -- the one behaviour the layered design exists to prevent.

payload.action: Scope a rule to the layer the FILE it governs lives in, not the layer that implements it. ports is now a declared layer carrying ARCH-007, ARCH-010 and TYPE-009.
payload.claim: ARCH-007 -- every port is a Protocol with a published contract -- was declared in edges.yaml as applying to the adapters layer only, so 'nav applies src/pkg/ports/clock.py', the most obvious question anyone would ask about a port, returned nothing about ports.

payload.action: Do not build a scoped gate on this shape. Measure step timings before optimising a gate; the intuition that many steps means slow was wrong by an order of magnitude.
payload.claim: The ten-step gate is 37.5s and the test suite is 30.9s of it -- 82%. Every other step together is 6.6s, so a scoped gate that skips untouched cheap steps saves about six seconds while introducing a gate that can narrow itself.

payload.action: When a decision is blocked because the corpus may not hold the value, put the value in project-owned space and check its USE rather than its content. Declare it, then be checked on it.
payload.claim: OPEN-006 was closable without resolving it: the tier-to-model table moved to overrides/allocation.toml, which is project-owned and never vendored, so the corpus still names no model while a check can require every dispatch to cite a tier the mapping resolves.

payload.action: A template's placeholder must be a sentinel the check refuses, not prose in the shape of an answer. Test the check against the real shipped template so the two cannot drift.
payload.claim: The allocation.toml template shipped plausible placeholders ('your-strongest-model'), which resolve -- so an adopter copying it unedited SATISFIED ALLOC-010. A check passed on a file nobody had read, in the repository whose whole subject is checks that decide nothing.

payload.action: Installing a tool is not wiring it. Run it against something, count what it examined, and check what the CONFIGURATION actually enables before crediting a rule to it.
payload.claim: Doxygen was installed, pinned and version-verified for a full release while the only invocation anywhere was --version; four rules were external on a tool that answered what version it was. Running it also showed DOC-007's auto:doxygen tag claimed a contribution the configuration cannot make.

payload.action: Resolve a mechanism tag against the mechanism's own claim, not against a filename. A rule can otherwise tag any check that exists and be counted decided; the headline number was overstated by twenty for a whole release.
payload.claim: V080 was 0 because mechanism_is_implemented asked whether a check MODULE existed, never whether that check claimed the rule. Eight checks named 17 rules they can never report -- five saying so in their own docstrings -- and four rules tagged check:domain_purity, which claims none of them. The true count of binding rules decided by nothing was 20.

payload.action: Give a mutation tree whatever it needs to satisfy every rule EXCEPT the one under test. A mutation that provokes two rules is evidence about neither.
payload.claim: A mutation for a rule decided by a multi-rule check must isolate that rule: the ALLOC entries provoked ALLOC-010 alongside because the synthetic tree had no allocation mapping, so no single entry could say which mechanism discriminated.

payload.action: When two rules state one obligation, retire one with a Superseded by field rather than keeping both. The id survives so an old citation still lands somewhere true.
payload.claim: ALLOC-008 and TEAMS-002 are the same rule -- same obligation, same rationale, same check, near-identical wording. Two ids for one obligation means a reader who greps either finds half the rule and believes it is the whole.

payload.action: Split undecided rules by whether a mechanism is POSSIBLE: advisory where it is a judgement, binding-and-unbuilt where it is merely unwritten. The corpus has both words and was using one for both cases.
payload.claim: A rule whose own check documents it as undecidable should be ADVISORY, not BINDING-and-unbuilt. ERR-011, ERR-014, TYPE-011 and TYPE-012 were BINDING while the checks naming them said in prose they could not decide them -- so the force tag promised a gate that would never fire.

payload.action: Treat V080 as a floor, not a count, until the discrimination matrix covers fitness-decided rules. The DISCIPLINE_REFERENCE seam now makes that possible.
payload.claim: 64 rules rest on a fitness: tag, which is resolved by asking whether a function of that name exists -- the same question that made V080 read 0 for two releases on the check side. A fitness function declares no rule list, so nothing can compare its claim against what it decides, and none of the 64 is discriminated.

payload.action: Assign sys.modules[spec.name] before calling exec_module, and pop it in a finally block.
payload.claim: importlib.util.module_from_spec loading a module that defines a slots dataclass dies with "'NoneType' object has no attribute '__dict__'", naming neither the module nor the cause, because the dataclass machinery resolves sys.modules[cls.__module__] to rebuild the class.

payload.action: Make every mechanism declare what it decides in a form a parser can read -- a rules tuple for a check, a @decides decorator for a fitness test -- and resolve the tag against the declaration, never against the file existing.
payload.claim: A mechanism tag resolved by the existence of a file or function counts a rule as decided that the mechanism never claimed; the check side was wrong for 17 of 73 rules and the fitness side for 16 of 64, both around 20-23%.

payload.action: Write a discrimination mutation for every auto: rule. The mutation is the only thing that can discover a rule whose tool was never told about it.
payload.claim: An auto: mechanism tag is unverifiable by construction -- mechanism_is_implemented returns None for it -- so four of the eight rules tagged auto:import-linter were named by no contract that runs, and V080 could never have said so.

payload.action: Author skills/python-discipline/SKILL.md, mirror it during discipline maintenance, vendor it once under .agent/skills, and let integrate.py manage each host path only when its record proves ownership.
payload.claim: A multi-host discipline needs one vendored skill authority; .claude and .agents copies are integration outputs whose replacement and removal require recorded ownership and content digests.

payload.action: Permit native stderr temporarily, capture LASTEXITCODE immediately, restore strict error handling, and decide the Conda transaction from that exit status.
payload.claim: On Windows PowerShell 5.1, a native Conda command can surface stderr as a NativeCommandError even though its process exit status is authoritative.

payload.action: Put the locked Node executable on PATH before invoking Pyright and require its global-Node mode in the container image.
payload.claim: Pyright can create a hidden Node environment when the declared Node executable is not on PATH before Pyright is invoked.

payload.action: Run the cache-aware Docker build on every launcher invocation so Docker reconciles the declared inputs before execution.
payload.claim: Inspecting only a pre-existing Docker image cannot prove that the image reflects the current Dockerfile, lock file, checker, and entrypoint inputs.

payload.note: The task concerned DOC integration; token measurement did not affect the roadmap.

payload.action: Treat local-binding documentation as a new v5 proposition with its own AST association mechanism and counterexamples instead of claiming DOC-002 already decides it.
payload.claim: The v4.1 kernel and DOC-002 describe every element or named value, but doc_coverage inspects only module and class assignments and never function-local bindings.

payload.action: Keep entity contracts and implementation narration in separate DOC modules and make each mechanism inspect only its owning comment form.
payload.claim: DOC-009 governs Doxygen entity contracts, while semantic implementation narration belongs in ordinary non-extracted comments, so the two comment forms do not make contradictory demands.
